brand.name: Break Free
brand.tagline: the frontier model leads, other models execute

videos.title: Why, what, and how
videos.subtitle: the frontier model leads, other models execute

lines.text: Your best model is the expensive one. Most of the work in a task is not the hard part.
Boilerplate, tests, migrations, docs, bulk edits: work that needs care, not genius.
Run all of it on a frontier model and you pay the top rate for typing.
Hand it to a cheap model instead and you get a confident report that nobody checked.
Break Free splits the job in two. The frontier model leads. Other models execute.
Claude Code or Codex keeps the judgement: understanding you, decomposing, designing, reviewing, owning the result.
DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, OpenRouter, or a local Ollama model does the execution.
They meet at one MCP server that you install once.
For every task the lead writes the instruction, the acceptance criteria, and the command that proves it.
The gateway runs that command itself, after the worker finishes. A pass is a real exit code, not a claim.
Independent tasks run at the same time as a dependency graph, and a failed check blocks whatever depended on it.
Workers are jailed: no shell, no force push, no protected branches, no secrets in a diff.
Every task, outcome and decision is written to a Markdown ledger in your repository, so the next session resumes instead of restarting.
One command installs it, and the setup walks you through the providers, the keys and the checks.

videos.title: Delegate one task
videos.subtitle: hand off the work, keep the verification

lines.text: You have a task that needs care, not genius. Unit tests for the router.
You tell the lead to delegate it, and you say how it will be proven.
The gateway sends it to a cheaper model with read, write and run, plus the test command.
The worker reports back, and the gateway runs the tests itself. Exit code zero, or the task failed.
You review a diff that has already been tested, and your frontier quota barely moved.

videos.title: Run a plan in parallel
videos.subtitle: a dependency graph, several vendors at once

lines.text: One feature is really four pieces of work: the core, its tests, the docs, and the wiring.
You describe them once, with what depends on what.
The core goes first. The moment its verification passes, the other three start together on different vendors.
A failing check fails that task and skips everything downstream. Nothing broken moves forward.
You get one consolidated report, with every verification result attached.

videos.title: Get an independent verdict
videos.subtitle: a different vendor reviews, a panel decides

lines.text: Before this lands, you want an opinion that is not the author's.
Review sends the real diff to a different vendor and asks for a verdict, not a compliment.
Back comes a structured answer: approve, revise or reject, with a file and a line for every issue.
For a decision rather than a diff, a panel runs several models at once and a judge synthesises them.
You still decide. You just decide with the disagreement in front of you.

videos.title: Resume across sessions
videos.subtitle: the ledger lives in the repository

lines.text: Context windows end. Projects do not.
Every task, decision and gotcha is written to plain Markdown inside your repository.
Commit it, review it in a pull request, or open the folder as an Obsidian vault.
Workers read it too, so a gotcha found once is not rediscovered by the next model.
Next session, resume reads the handoff and tells you exactly where you were.
